source_text:
Ἐγράψατέ μοι καὶ ὑμεῖς καὶ Ἰγνάτιος, ἵν᾽, ἐάν τις ἀπέρχηται εἰς Συρίαν, καὶ τὰ παῤ ὑμῶν ἀποκομίσῃ γράμματα: ὅπερ ποιήσω,ἐὰν λάβω καιρὸν εὔθετον, εἴτε ἐγώ, εἴτε ὄν πέμπω πρεσβεύσοντα καὶ περὶ ὑμῶν.
τὰς ἐπιστολὰς Ἰγνατίου τὰς πεμφθείσας ἡμῖν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἄλλας, ὅσας εἴχομεν παῤ ἡμῖν, ἐπέμψαμεν ὑμῖν, καθὼς ἐνετείλασθε: αἵτινες ὑποτεταγμέναι εἰσὶν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ ταύτῃ, ἐξ ὧν μεγάλα ὠφεληθῆναι δυνήσεσθε. περιέχουσι γὰρ πίστιν καὶ ὑπομονὴν καὶ πᾶσαν οἰκοδομὴν τὴν εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἀνήκουσαν. Et de ipso Ignatio et de his, qui cum eo sunt, quod certius agnoveritis, significate.
thought_title: Forwarding letters to Syria and sending Ignatius's letters
orientation: Polycarp is writing to the Philippians about letters: he will forward theirs to Syria when he can, and he has sent them the letters of Ignatius that he had.
pass_a_gloss: You wrote to me, both you and Ignatius, that, if anyone goes to Syria, he should also carry the letters from you; which I will do, if I get a suitable time, either I myself, or the one whom I send to be an ambassador also concerning you. The letters of Ignatius, the ones sent to us by him, and others, as many as we had with us, we sent to you, just as you commanded; which are attached to this letter, from which you will be able to be greatly benefited. For they contain faith and endurance and all edification that pertains to our Lord. And concerning Ignatius himself and concerning those who are with him, what you may know more certainly, report it.

choices.why: The verb means to act as an envoy or ambassador; the participle indicates the role of the one sent.
The letters are placed under or appended to this letter, so 'attached' fits the physical sense.
The noun means building up, used metaphorically for spiritual edification.
The participle means reaching up to or belonging to, so 'pertains' captures the relation to the Lord.
The Latin imperative means to make known or report; the context is asking for news about Ignatius.

pass_b_english: You and Ignatius both wrote to me asking that if anyone is going to Syria, he should also carry your letters there. I will do this, if I find a suitable opportunity, either myself or through someone I send to be an ambassador on your behalf as well.

We have sent you the letters of Ignatius that he sent to us, along with all the others we had with us, just as you instructed. They are attached to this letter, and you will be able to gain great benefit from them, for they contain faith, endurance, and every kind of edification that pertains to our Lord. And regarding Ignatius himself and those who are with him, report to us whatever you learn with greater certainty.

last_rejected.quote: We have sent you the letters of Ignatius that he sent to us, along with all the others we had with us, just as you instructed.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'as you instructed' — the English does include this. Checking again: it is present. Disregard.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'just as you instructed' renders καθὼς ἐνετείλασθε accurately; no omission.
